name: How Do I Prevent Cabinet and Tile Delays From Extending a San Diego Remodel?

mainEntity.name: What materials should be ordered first to prevent delays during a kitchen renovation?
mainEntity.text: What materials should be ordered first to prevent delays during a kitchen renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: The delay risk is highest for custom or made-to-order items, including cabinets, specialty appliances, stone, custom tile, hardware, decorative lighting, and unusual plumbing fixtures. Start with an approved selections schedule that includes product names, model numbers, colors, quantities, lead times, and backup choices. Confirm availability directly with the supplier and ask whether the quoted date is an estimate or a guaranteed ship date. Verify that materials can be stored safely and that the site is ready for delivery. Inspect cabinets and appliances promptly for damage or shortages; do not wait until installation day to discover missing fillers, panels, trim, or hardware. Tie demolition and rough construction to material milestones. A contractor should explain which work can proceed without creating rework and which tasks depend on final products. Include written responsibility for expedited shipping, incorrect quantities, damaged goods, and owner-caused substitutions. Local project reviews frequently describe tile shortages, cabinet delays, and changing completion estimates, so a procurement plan and weekly status update can protect the schedule.
acceptedAnswer.description: Order items with long or uncertain lead times first, usually cabinets, specialty appliances, countertops, custom hardware, tile, windows, and lighting. Confirm availability in writing, keep approved alternates, and coordinate delivery with storage and site readiness. Do not begin irreversible demolition until critical materials and measurements are confirmed.
